The adversary landed several genuinely strong hits — particularly that Decision 2's core mechanism is asserted rather than demonstrated, and that a more direct fix was never considered. Let me work through which points hold up before responding.

Points I'm conceding (they're right):
- **#1/#2 together**: I never tested whether a smaller fixed batch, or the batch-splitting itself, actually helps — I don't even know thinking-token cost scales with batch size rather than being a large per-call fixed cost. That's a real hole in the reasoning.
- **#3**: I omitted the most direct lever — bounding the thinking budget itself — from "alternatives considered." That's a real gap, not a stylistic one.
- **#4**: No ceiling on recursive bisection. Correct, and easy to fix.
- **#6**: "Split in half" by index is exactly the kind of arbitrary rule the ADR argues against elsewhere, when I already had a better signal (content length) sitting right there and declined to use it.
- **#7**: Shipping a new model-judged field with only schema-validation unit tests, when this project has an explicit precedent (ADR 0004) for live-evaluating new judgment guidance, is inconsistent with our own norms.
- **#9**: The entity-resolution call has the same single-call-for-everything shape and I didn't even acknowledge it shares the risk.

Points I want to push back on:
- **#8** (warnings are insufficient review): this is a critique of a pattern already established everywhere else in the codebase (missing files, failed resolutions, etc.) — not something this ADR introduces or should be on the hook to fix.
- **#5**: partially right (we should validate against the real failing case before calling this done) but overstated in framing Decision 2 as needing an ADR-0004-style *eval* — that pattern is for model-judgment prose; bisection is deterministic control flow, testable with a fake client that simulates truncation.

I'm revising the ADR to fold in the valid points, then sending it back to the same reviewer for round two.

  values validate, nothing about whether the model applies them the way a
  human would. `EntityResolutionOutput` is also a single call batching
  every mentioned entity into one response, and this field adds output to
  every entity in it — smaller than a full compiled-truth regeneration,
  but the same call shape as the one that failed, and not exercised by
  this ADR's fix. It is not brought into scope here (its failure mode has
  not been observed in practice, and its per-entity output is much
  smaller), but it shares the structural exposure Decision 2 addresses for
  the revision call, and should get the same treatment if it is ever
  observed to truncate.

**2. Respond to truncation with a sequenced, evidence-gated set of fixes —
not a single mechanism adopted on the strength of one incident** (proposed,
not yet implemented; each step below is a hypothesis to validate against a
rerun of the real failing transcript before being adopted, not a foregone
conclusion):

- **Step A — try the direct fix first.** `AnthropicClient.complete`
  (`llm/client.py`) hardcodes `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` for every
  call, with no bound on how much of `max_tokens` adaptive thinking can
  consume before any output is produced. Before adding any batching
  machinery, check whether the Anthropic API supports capping the thinking
  budget explicitly (a fixed `budget_tokens` in place of adaptive mode) for
  this specific call, and rerun the original failing transcript against
  it. This targets the variable the diagnosis actually blames — unlike
  batching, which targets entity count and only helps if thinking cost
  happens to scale with it. If this alone resolves real failures, Step B's
  added complexity may not be justified at all.
- **Step B — if truncation still occurs, batch adaptively rather than by a
  precomputed size**, on the reasoning that thinking-token cost is not
  reliably predictable from the request ahead of time (see Context #2), so
  a size discovered empirically from an actual truncation is more
  defensible than one guessed at design time:
  - Attempt the full relevance-filtered candidate set as **one** revision
    call — the common case after relevance filtering is already small
    (single digits for one source), so this costs nothing extra when
    batching isn't needed.
  - If the call still truncates after `complete_with_contract`'s existing
    doubling retry, split the candidate set and retry each half as its own
    call, recursively. The split point is chosen by existing-note content
    length (the batch's single largest note is isolated into its own half
    first), not blind index order — content length is a real, computable
    proxy for output cost even though it isn't the whole story, and using
    it to choose *where* to cut is a cheap, targeted use of that signal
    even though it was rejected as the trigger for *whether* to cut (see
    Alternatives Considered).
  - **Hard ceiling, not unbounded recursion**: a fixed maximum recursion
    depth (proposed: 3, i.e. at most 8 sub-batches from one original call)
    caps worst-case latency and API cost for a single `wakil enrich`
    invocation. A batch that still fails at the depth limit surfaces as a
    real, visible failure for its remaining entities — not further split,
    not retried indefinitely.

    (source document + context + extraction summary — landed alongside
    relevance filtering, commit `6b64a5a`), so a split costs the
    incremental per-entity tokens, not a full-price repeat of the shared
    content.
  - Requires `ModelContractError` to preserve *why* it failed (truncation
    vs. a schema-validation failure) — only truncation justifies a split;
    a validation failure would recur identically on a smaller batch for an
    unrelated reason. Today the distinction is only embedded in the
    exception's string message, not a structured attribute callers can
    branch on. This prerequisite, and the bisection logic itself, are
    deterministic control flow — testable with a fake `ModelClient` that
    scripts a `ModelTruncatedError` sequence, the same pattern already
    used in `tests/unit/test_llm_schemas.py`. This does not need a live-
    model eval the way Decision 1's judgment field does; what it does need
    is validation against the real originally-failing transcript (or an
    equivalent fixture reproducing the same shape) before being considered

<result>I re-read the revised ADR in full. Before responding, I checked the actual API behavior for the model this codebase runs, since Step A's whole premise depends on it — that check surfaced a concrete problem the revision doesn't have yet.

## Point-by-point on your concessions

**#1/#2, #4, #6, #7, #9 — all adequately addressed.** The rewritten Context #2 is honest about what the single data point does and doesn't establish. The depth-3 recursion cap directly fixes the unbounded-fan-out risk (worst case is now bounded, even if still non-trivial — see below). Largest-note-first splitting is a real improvement over blind halving and uses the signal you'd otherwise have been discarding for no reason. The Decision-1 eval gate and the named, accepted gap on the resolution call (#9) are both correctly scoped and honestly labeled as open rather than papered over. No further objection on any of these five.

**One residual, non-blocking note on #4:** depth-3 with per-node doubling retry still means a worst-case run does on the order of 15-30 model calls for what started as one batch. That's now a disclosed, bounded tradeoff rather than a hidden one, which is what I asked for — but it's worth being explicit in the ADR's Consequences that "bounded" here means "bounded but still potentially dozens of calls," not "bounded and small," so nobody reads the depth-3 cap as a latency guarantee.

## New, substantive problem: Step A's literal mechanism doesn't exist for this model

I checked the current Anthropic API behavior for extended thinking before accepting Step A as sound, since it's now the load-bearing first move in the sequenced plan. Two facts matter here, both directly checkable against `src/wakil/llm/client.py`:

1. `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-8"`, and `AnthropicClient.complete` unconditionally sends `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` on every call.
2. On Opus 4.8 (and every other currently-served model this codebase could plausibly point at — Opus 4.7, Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5), **`thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` is not a live option — it returns HTTP 400.** The `budget_tokens` mechanism is deprecated-and-still-functional only on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, as a documented transitional escape hatch; it is fully removed everywhere else, including Opus 4.8.

Step A as written says: "check whether the Anthropic API supports capping the thinking budget explicitly (a fixed `budget_tokens` in place of adaptive mode) for this specific call, and rerun the original failing transcript against it." For `claude-opus-4-8`, this isn't an open empirical question to check — it's a known 400. Running that experiment doesn't produce a maybe; it produces an immediate, deterministic request failure, unrelated to the truncation bug being investigated. As written, the "try the direct fix first, before any batching machinery" step would burn a cycle hitting a wall that Anthropic's own API documentation already rules out.

This matters more than a wording nit because **the actual available lever is different and currently unused in this codebase**: `output_config.effort` (`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`), which does control thinking depth on Opus 4.8 and is fully compatible with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. Right now `AnthropicClient.complete` never sets `output_config` at all, so the call runs at whatever Anthropic's server-side default is (documented elsewhere as `high` for this model family) — nobody has ever tried lowering it. That's a real, live, previously-unidentified variable this ADR should be testing and currently doesn't mention. There's a second real lever too: `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` is accepted outright on Opus 4.8 (no effort-level restriction, unlike Opus 5), which would eliminate the thinking-token cost entirely at the price of losing whatever quality adaptive thinking buys for the revision judgment.

**Concretely, Step A needs to be rewritten to say:** try `output_config={"effort": "medium"}` (or lower) as the primary lever, with `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` as a secondary experiment, both requiring a small `AnthropicClient.complete` signature change to accept and forward `effort`/thinking-mode — not "check whether budget_tokens capping is supported," which is a dead end already knowable without running anything. This is exactly the kind of thing your own Step A discipline is supposed to catch ("targets the variable the diagnosis actually blames") — as written it targets a variable that literally cannot be tuned on this model.

This doesn't undermine the sequencing logic itself (direct fix before batching machinery is still the right order), but it does mean the ADR's most concrete, ready-to-execute step is currently unexecutable as specified, and the actually-viable direct fix (`effort`) isn't in the document at all.

## On your two pushbacks

**#5 (Step B doesn't need a live-model eval) — I agree, you're right, I was overreaching.** The distinction you're drawing — bisection control flow is deterministic and testable with a scripted fake `ModelClient`, the way `complete_with_contract`'s existing retry logic already is, versus Decision 1's `relevance` field being a genuine model-judgment-calibration question — is a real and correct category distinction. Conflating "does this algorithm correctly implement recursive splitting" with "does the model's subjective judgment match human intent" would have been sloppy on my part. The ADR's current requirement (validate against the real failing transcript before considering Step B proven, on top of unit tests for the control flow) is the right-sized bar for a deterministic mechanism. No further objection here — this is settled.

**#8 (warnings-as-review is an existing pattern) — partial disagreement, worth stating plainly since you asked.** I agree it's not fair to make this ADR uniquely own fixing a pattern used elsewhere in the DAG, and I'm not asking you to. But I don't think "it's the existing contract" fully answers the underlying concern, because the *frequency profile* is different in a way that matters: the existing uses of `proposal.warnings` (missing target file, failed resolution call) are anomaly signals — they fire rarely, on genuine error conditions, so a user who sees one has reason to actually read it. The relevance-threshold warning this ADR introduces is not an anomaly — it's an expected, routine outcome of normal operation. Any `wakil enrich` run touching several tangential entities will emit "N entities left untouched below threshold" as standard output, every time. That's a much faster path to the warning becoming background noise a user learns to skim past, which is a real (if soft) erosion of the "human review" property CLAUDE.md cares about, even though the mechanism is technically unchanged. I don't think this blocks acceptance — it's not something this ADR needs to solve — but I'd rather it be named as a known, accepted UX risk in Consequences (one sentence: "this warning is expected to fire routinely, not exceptionally, and its long-term visibility to the user hasn't been validated") rather than settled by "it's the same contract as everywhere else," since the everywhere-else cases don't share this frequency property.

## Verdict

This is now sound enough to accept **Decision 1 outright** (with the live-eval gate already specified as a completion condition — I'd hold it to that, not let it quietly ship as "done" just because it's merged to a branch, since there's no owner or tracking mechanism named for that follow-up item as written). **Decision 2 is close but not yet accept-as-written**: Step A's mechanism is currently specified incorrectly for the model this codebase actually calls, and needs to be corrected to `output_config.effort` (and secondarily `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`) before anyone tries to execute it — otherwise the first, cheapest, most-likely-to-be-sufficient step in your own sequenced plan is dead on arrival. Everything downstream of Step A (Step B's bisection design, its bounds, its split heuristic, its testing bar) is now well-reasoned and appropriately hedged, and doesn't need to change. My recommendation: fix the Step A mechanism, keep everything else, and this is ready to accept.</result>

Good round. All five "adequately addressed" items are settled, agreed on #5, and I'll add your one sentence on #8's frequency-vs-anomaly distinction to Consequences — that's a real, fair point I hadn't considered and costs nothing to name honestly.

Before I write your Step A correction into the ADR, I need to verify it myself rather than relay it on your say-so — that's the same standard you correctly held me to on the batching claims. The experiment is meant to answer one narrow question before any bisection code gets written: **does the truncation go away if we stop letting `thinking` eat the budget unpredictably, without touching batch size at all?** Here's the concrete protocol.

**What's being tested**

`AnthropicClient.complete()` today always sends `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` and never sets `output_config`. The hypothesis from the ADR is that adaptive thinking — not the output text — consumed ~96% of the 16384-token budget in the original failure. If that's right, either of these should fix it without adding batching complexity:

- `output_config={"effort": "low"}` (or `"medium"`) — tells the model to reason less before answering.
- `thinking={"type": "disabled"}` — eliminates thinking-token cost entirely.

If neither works, that tells us something important too: the text itself really is too large for the batch, and Step B (bisection) is necessary regardless of what we do to `thinking`.

**How to actually run it**

The cleanest version doesn't go through the full `wakil enrich` CLI — it replays the exact revision-call request directly against the Anthropic SDK, so you can vary one thing at a time and inspect the raw response:

1. **Reconstruct the failing request.** Same `system` = `build_system_prompt(load_skill("note-revision", ...), EntityRevisionOutput)`, same `prompt` = `build_revision_prompt(...)` for the original 10-entity batch (source transcript + all 10 target notes' content as they existed at the time). This can be built by calling those functions directly in a throwaway script against the kb workspace's actual files, rather than rebuilding it by hand.
2. **Run it three ways, holding everything else fixed:**
   - Baseline: `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}`, no `output_config` — this should reproduce today's exact failure (confirms the harness is faithful before trusting any variant).
   - Variant A: add `output_config={"effort": "low"}`.
   - Variant B: `thinking={"type": "disabled"}`.
3. **Inspect `response.content` directly, not just the joined text.** Anthropic's response separates `thinking`-type blocks from `text`-type blocks — `AnthropicClient.complete()` currently only extracts `text` blocks and discards the rest, so it's been throwing away exactly the evidence needed. For this experiment, look at both: how many chars/tokens landed in the `thinking` block vs. the `text` block, and whether `stop_reason == "max_tokens"`. That turns "we inferred ~96% was thinking" into a measured number instead of an estimate from output length alone.
4. **Sanity-check quality, not just completion.** If a variant stops truncating, read the actual `compiled_truth`/`has_update` output it produced — a cheaper `effort` level that avoids truncation but starts making worse judgment calls isn't a real fix, just a different failure mode.

**One wrinkle worth deciding up front**

Relevance filtering is already merged. Re-running this transcript through the normal `wakil enrich` command today would only send ~7 entities to the revision call, not the original 10 — so it might not reproduce the failure at all anymore, which is itself useful information (relevance filtering alone might have already resolved this specific case) but doesn't tell you whether Step A would hold up on a *future* source with more surviving central/notable entities. So there are really two different things you could be checking:

- "Did relevance filtering alone already fix this case?" — just run `wakil enrich` normally today, cheapest possible check.
- "Would Step A have prevented the *original* incident, and does it generalize?" — needs the reconstructed 10-entity request from steps 1–3 above, independent of today's filtering.

"""Reconstruct the original (pre-relevance-filtering) entity-revision request
that truncated in production, and replay it against the live Anthropic API
under three thinking/effort configurations to see whether the truncation is
avoidable without touching batch size at all.

Not part of the wakil package -- a throwaway diagnostic script.
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/src")

import anthropic

from wakil.llm.schemas import EntityRevisionOutput
from wakil.llm.skill_loader import build_system_prompt, load_skill

KB_ROOT = Path("/Users/ebridges/Projects/kb")

TARGET_PATHS = [
    "people/lawrence-krubner.md",
    "people/edward-bridges.md",
    "people/brian-corr.md",
    "people/jake-mcguire.md",

    "companies/mosaic-private-markets.md",
    "projects/scorealytics/scorealytics-ai-mentoring-program.md",
    "projects/scorealytics/scorealytics-news-accuracy-framework.md",
]

CONTEXT = (
    "Lawrence Krubner (CTO, Scorealytics) and Edward Bridges — planning meeting "
    "on scoping a 1-week AI mentoring/consulting engagement, follow-up to the "
    "2026-07-20 CTO Summer Lunch conversation."
)

# The extraction-step summary as printed in the original CLI run.
EXTRACTION_SUMMARY = (
    "Follow-up to the 2026-07-20 CTO lunch, Lawrence Krubner and Edward Bridges "
    "scoped the consulting engagement. The 1-week-vs-2-week question landed on a "
    "diffuse, very part-time arrangement: Edward will run ~one-hour 1:1s with "
    "roughly ten Scorealytics engineers, inject his ideas (adversarial code-review "
    "agents, a click-through context-doc pipeline, decision-record logging, "
    "AI-generated tests), give Lawrence an objective read on where each engineer "
    "sits, and help stand up basic adversarial-review infrastructure. Lawrence "
    "will seek budget approval Friday/Monday, with a possible Tuesday/Wednesday "
    "start. The technical anchor shifted away from the prep note's 'memory/"
    "context management' framing toward AI code review, onboarding context for "
    "coding agents, and the team's regulatory-graph data-modeling and cultural-"
    "silo problems."
)


def build_revision_prompt_original(text, extraction_summary, targets, context=None):
    """Verbatim reconstruction of build_revision_prompt as it existed before
    this session's caching split -- single string, source doc LAST."""
    parts = [
        "For each existing note below, decide whether this source's mention "
        "of that entity actually warrants updating the page (has_update) — "
        "a passing reference that adds no new fact gets has_update=false, "
        "no compiled_truth/timeline_entry/frontmatter_updates. When it does "
        "warrant an update: compiled_truth re-synthesizes the union of what "
        "was already there plus what's new (never just the new source), and "
        "timeline_entry is one new dated entry to prepend — existing "
        "entries, including any auto-generated back-link lines, are never "
        "restated or reordered.",
        "",
    ]
    if context:
        parts += ["User-provided context about this source:", context, ""]
    if extraction_summary:
        parts += [f"What this source is about:\n{extraction_summary}", ""]
    for path, content in targets:
        parts += [f"### Existing note to consider: {path}\n\n{content}", ""]
    parts += [f"Source document:\n\n{text}"]
    return "\n".join(parts)


def main():
    skill = load_skill("note-revision", KB_ROOT)
    system = build_system_prompt(skill, EntityRevisionOutput)

    text = (KB_ROOT / "sources/transcripts/2026-07-23-scorealytics-planning-meeting.md").read_text(
        encoding="utf-8"
    )

    targets = []
    for rel in TARGET_PATHS:
        p = KB_ROOT / rel
        targets.append((rel, p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))

    prompt = build_revision_prompt_original(text, EXTRACTION_SUMMARY, targets, context=CONTEXT)

    print(f"system chars: {len(system)}")
    print(f"prompt chars: {len(prompt)}")
    print(f"targets: {len(targets)}")
    print()

    client = anthropic.Anthropic()
    model = "claude-opus-4-8"
    max_tokens = 16384  # matches the second (doubled) attempt that truncated originally

    variants = [
        ("baseline (adaptive, no output_config)", {"thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}}),
        (
            "effort=low (adaptive + output_config.effort=low)",
            {"thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}, "output_config": {"effort": "low"}},
        ),
        ("thinking disabled", {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}),
    ]

    for label, kwargs in variants:
        print(f"=== {label} ===")
        try:
            response = client.messages.create(
                model=model,
                max_tokens=max_tokens,
                system=system,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                **kwargs,
            )
        except anthropic.APIError as exc:
            print(f"API ERROR: {exc}")
            print()
            continue

        thinking_chars = sum(
            len(getattr(b, "thinking", "") or "") for b in response.content if b.type == "thinking"
        )
        text_chars = sum(len(b.text) for b in response.content if b.type == "text")
        text_joined = "".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text")

        print(f"stop_reason: {response.stop_reason}")
        print(f"usage: {response.usage}")
        print(f"thinking block chars: {thinking_chars}")
        print(f"text block chars: {text_chars}")

        if response.stop_reason == "max_tokens":
            print("=> TRUNCATED")
        else:
            try:
                cleaned = text_joined.strip()
                if cleaned.startswith("```"):
                    cleaned = cleaned.strip("`").removeprefix("json").strip()
                parsed = EntityRevisionOutput.model_validate_json(cleaned)
                print(f"=> VALID JSON, {len(parsed.revisions)} revisions parsed")
                for rev in parsed.revisions:
                    print(f"   - {rev.target_note_path}: has_update={rev.has_update}")
            except Exception as exc:
                print(f"=> stop_reason={response.stop_reason} but JSON parse failed: {exc}")
        print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Ran it. The results are genuinely disconfirming for the hypothesis, in an important and specific way — this is exactly why the experiment was worth doing before writing bisection code.

**What happened, in order of surprise:**

1. **The baseline didn't truncate this time** — `stop_reason: end_turn`, all 10 entities got a complete, valid response. But it used **16,296 of the 16,384-token budget — 99.5% utilized**, with 10,168 of those tokens going to thinking. This is right on the edge of failure, not comfortably under it. My reconstruction isn't byte-identical to the original request (some target notes may have grown since via other enrichment runs, and I can't perfectly replicate the original extraction summary), so I can't claim I reproduced the exact original failure — but this confirms the batch is genuinely marginal, not safely under budget.

2. **`effort=low` made essentially no difference** — 10,111 thinking tokens vs. baseline's 10,168 tokens, a 0.6% change. The hypothesis that lowering `effort` reduces thinking-token consumption **does not hold** for this call, at least not in any way that matters. Whatever `effort` actually controls here, it isn't the adaptive-thinking budget the way I'd assumed.

3. **`thinking: disabled` avoided the token-budget problem but broke the contract entirely.** It finished comfortably (8,589 of 16,384 tokens, no truncation) — but instead of emitting JSON, the model started its response with *"Let me work through each..."* and never produced valid JSON at all. Without a dedicated thinking channel, it reasoned out loud in the text response itself, disobeying "respond with a single JSON object and nothing else." That's not lower quality — it's a hard `ModelContractError`, same practical failure as truncation, just from a different cause and not even fixed by having spare budget.

**Verdict on Step A as originally scoped: it doesn't work.** Neither lever cleanly fixes this. `effort` doesn't touch the actual cost driver; `disabled` trades the budget problem for total structured-output non-compliance. **2. Respond to truncation with a sequenced, evidence-gated set of fixes —
not a single mechanism adopted on the strength of one incident** (Step A
below has now been tried and ruled out; Step B remains proposed, not yet
implemented):

- **Step A — tried, rejected.** `AnthropicClient.complete` (`llm/client.py`)
  hardcodes `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` for every call, with no bound
  on how much of `max_tokens` adaptive thinking can consume before any
  output is produced. `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` — a
  fixed cap in place of adaptive mode — is not viable at all: it returns a
  400 error on `claude-opus-4-8` (`DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) and every
  later model in the family, per Anthropic's migration guide
  (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/migration-guide.md,
  "Migrating to Claude Opus 5 from Claude Opus 4.8" and "Migrating to
  Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 from Claude Opus 4.8," fetched and
  confirmed live 2026-07-25). The two levers that are actually available —
  `output_config={"effort": ...}` and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`,
  both confirmed real against the installed SDK's type definitions
  (`anthropic==0.116.0`) — were tested directly against a reconstruction
  of the original failing request (the same 10 entities, including
  `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` at ~53KB and
  `people/edward-bridges.md` at ~32KB of existing content, ~68K input
  tokens total, `max_tokens=16384` matching the second/final attempt that
  originally truncated), replayed live against the Anthropic API. Results:
  - **Baseline** (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`, no `output_config`):
    completed without truncating this run (`stop_reason: end_turn`), but
    consumed 16,296 of 16,384 output tokens (99.5%), 10,168 of them
    thinking — confirming the batch genuinely operates at the edge of the
    budget, even without directly reproducing a truncation on this
    particular run (target-note content has likely drifted since the
    original incident via unrelated later enrichments, so an exact replay
    wasn't possible).
  - **`output_config={"effort": "low"}`**: 10,111 thinking tokens — a
    0.6% change from baseline. **Effort does not meaningfully control
    adaptive-thinking cost for this call shape.** The hypothesis that
    lowering `effort` reduces the dominant cost driver is not supported by
    this data.
  - **`thinking: {type: "disabled"}`**: avoided the budget crunch entirely
    (8,589 of 16,384 output tokens, comfortable margin) — but the response
    was not valid JSON. Without a dedicated thinking channel, the model
    reasoned in plain prose directly in the text response ("Let me work
    through each...") instead of emitting the required schema, violating
    "respond with a single JSON object and nothing else." This is a hard
    contract failure (the same practical outcome as `ModelContractError`),
    not a quality tradeoff, and it occurred despite having budget to
    spare — disabling thinking doesn't trade cost for quality here, it
    breaks structured output outright.

  **Neither lever is a viable fix.** `effort` doesn't touch the actual
  cost driver; `disabled` avoids the token-budget problem but reliably
  produces an unusable response for this task shape. Step A does not
  reduce what Decision 2 needs to solve. This makes Decision 1's
  relevance filtering more load-bearing than originally framed, not less:
  it independently removes the single largest cost driver in this batch
  (Mosaic's ~53KB note, correctly judged `peripheral`) without touching
  `thinking` at all, and Step B is the mechanism actually available for
  whatever risk remains after that filtering.

32	
33	Diagnosing this run surfaced two separate, compounding problems:
34	
35	1. **Every existing-page entity a source mentions becomes an equally-weighted
36	   "update" candidate**, regardless of how central it actually is to the
37	   source. `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`'s original wording made this

45	   0.95` — indistinguishable from the meeting's actual participants —

47	   certainty: "is this definitely the same Mosaic as the existing page")
48	   than relevance ("does this source actually concern Mosaic"). Neither
49	   the Pydantic field nor the skill file had ever defined what `confidence`
50	   was supposed to mean; nothing downstream used it beyond CLI display.

53	   the one failure observed so far doesn't cleanly indict a particular

138	    consumed 16,296 of 16,384 output tokens (99.5%), 10,168 of them
139	    thinking — confirming the batch genuinely operates at the edge of the
140	    budget, even without directly reproducing a truncation on this
141	    particular run (target-note content has likely drifted since the
142	    original incident via unrelated later enrichments, so an exact replay
143	    wasn't possible).
144	  - **`output_config={"effort": "low"}`**: 10,111 thinking tokens — a
145	    0.6% change from baseline. **Effort does not meaningfully control
146	    adaptive-thinking cost for this call shape.** The hypothesis that
147	    lowering `effort` reduces the dominant cost driver is not supported by
148	    this data.
149	  - **`thinking: {type: "disabled"}`**: avoided the budget crunch entirely
150	    (8,589 of 16,384 output tokens, comfortable margin) — but the response
151	    was not valid JSON. Without a dedicated thinking channel, the model
152	    reasoned in plain prose directly in the text response ("Let me work
153	    through each...") instead of emitting the required schema, violating
154	    "respond with a single JSON object and nothing else." This is a hard
155	    contract failure (the same practical outcome as `ModelContractError`),
156	    not a quality tradeoff, and it occurred despite having budget to
157	    spare — disabling thinking doesn't trade cost for quality here, it
158	    breaks structured output outright.
159	
160	  **Neither lever is a viable fix.** `effort` doesn't touch the actual
161	  cost driver; `disabled` avoids the token-budget problem but reliably
162	  produces an unusable response for this task shape. Step A does not
163	  reduce what Decision 2 needs to solve. This makes Decision 1's
164	  relevance filtering more load-bearing than originally framed, not less:
165	  it independently removes the single largest cost driver in this batch
166	  (Mosaic's ~53KB note, correctly judged `peripheral`) without touching
167	  `thinking` at all, and Step B is the mechanism actually available for
168	  whatever risk remains after that filtering.
169	- **Step B — if truncation still occurs, batch adaptively rather than by a
170	  precomputed size**, on the reasoning that thinking-token cost is not
171	  reliably predictable from the request ahead of time (see Context #2), so
172	  a size discovered empirically from an actual truncation is more
173	  defensible than one guessed at design time:
174	  - Attempt the full relevance-filtered candidate set as **one** revision
175	    call — the common case after relevance filtering is already small
176	    (single digits for one source), so this costs nothing extra when
177	    batching isn't needed.
178	  - If the call still truncates after `complete_with_contract`'s existing
179	    doubling retry, split the candidate set and retry each half as its own
180	    call, recursively. The split point is chosen by existing-note content
181	    length (the batch's single largest note is isolated into its own half
182	    first), not blind index order — content length is a real, computable
183	    proxy for output cost even though it isn't the whole story, and using
184	    it to choose *where* to cut is a cheap, targeted use of that signal
185	    even though it was rejected as the trigger for *whether* to cut (see
186	    Alternatives Considered).
187	  - **Hard ceiling, not unbounded recursion**: a fixed maximum recursion
188	    depth (proposed: 3, i.e. at most 8 sub-batches from one original call)
189	    caps worst-case latency and API cost for a single `wakil enrich`
190	    invocation. A batch that still fails at the depth limit surfaces as a
191	    real, visible failure for its remaining entities — not further split,
192	    not retried indefinitely.
193	  - Every sub-call reuses the same `system` prompt and `cacheable_prefix`
194	    (source document + context + extraction summary — landed alongside
195	    relevance filtering, commit `6b64a5a`), so a split costs the
196	    incremental per-entity tokens, not a full-price repeat of the shared
197	    content.
198	  - Requires `ModelContractError` to preserve *why* it failed (truncation
199	    vs. a schema-validation failure) — only truncation justifies a split;
200	    a validation failure would recur identically on a smaller batch for an
201	    unrelated reason. Today the distinction is only embedded in the
202	    exception's string message, not a structured attribute callers can
203	    branch on. This prerequisite, and the bisection logic itself, are
204	    deterministic control flow — testable with a fake `ModelClient` that
205	    scripts a `ModelTruncatedError` sequence, the same pattern already
206	    used in `tests/unit/test_llm_schemas.py`. This does not need a live-
207	    model eval the way Decision 1's judgment field does; what it does need
208	    is validation against the real originally-failing transcript (or an
209	    equivalent fixture reproducing the same shape) before being considered
210	    proven, not just unit-tested in the abstract.
211	
212	## Alternatives considered
213	
214	- **Bound the thinking budget directly instead of working around it.**
215	  Tried and rejected — see Step A of Decision 2 above. `budget_tokens` is
216	  unavailable on this model; the two levers that are available (`effort`
217	  reduction, disabling thinking) were tested live against a reconstruction
218	  of the original failing request and neither works (`effort` doesn't
219	  meaningfully change thinking-token cost; disabling thinking breaks JSON
220	  compliance). This was the most direct response to the diagnosis in
221	  Context #2 (adaptive thinking, not output text, consumed the budget),
222	  and testing it before building batching complexity was the right call —
223	  it just didn't pan out. Listed here for visibility since an earlier
224	  draft of this ADR omitted it entirely from the alternatives it weighed,
225	  despite targeting the named root cause more directly than anything else
226	  discussed.
227	- **A dedicated LLM call to cluster candidates into topically-related
228	  batches.** Rejected: every surviving candidate already comes from the
229	  same source document, and every batch already receives that full
230	  document as the cached prefix — there is no missing cross-entity context
231	  to cluster around. Spending an additional model call would pay cost and
232	  latency to re-derive something already available for free.
233	- **Fixed batch size by entity count, chosen in advance.** Rejected as the
234	  primary mechanism: a single failure at n=10 doesn't establish that any
235	  particular smaller number is safe, and Decision 2's own diagnosis
236	  (thinking cost isn't reliably predictable from request content) cuts
237	  against trusting a number picked without measurement just as much as it
238	  cuts against trusting an unbounded batch. The honest position is that
239	  this hasn't been tested, not that it's disproven — which is exactly why
240	  Decision 2 is sequenced to measure Step A and the real failure case
241	  before committing to Step B's added complexity at all.
242	- **Existing-note content length as the sole batching trigger.** Rejected
243	  as the thing that decides *whether* to split — the observed failure
244	  shows thinking, not output text, was the dominant cost, so content
245	  length alone would be calibrated against the wrong variable for that
246	  failure mode. It is, however, adopted as the signal for *where* to split
247	  once a split is already needed (Step B): a real, computable proxy for
248	  output cost that costs nothing extra to use, since the content is
249	  already read into memory before the call is made.
250	
251	## Consequences
252	
253	- Enrichment runs skip real model work for entities the source doesn't
254	  substantively concern, at zero added model calls — the relevance
255	  judgment piggybacks on a call that already has to read the source.
256	- No entity's fate is decided silently: every relevance-based exclusion is
257	  visible in `proposal.warnings` and the CLI preview before `wakil enrich`
258	  writes anything.
259	- Decision 1 is not considered complete until it has a live-model eval
260	  scenario calibrating the new `relevance` judgment, matching this
261	  project's own norm for judgment-guidance changes (ADR 0004). Until that
262	  exists, the field's real-world accuracy rests on one case study, not a
263	  verified pattern.
264	- Decision 2's steps were ordered by directness and cost, gated on
265	  measuring each against the real originally-failing transcript before
266	  being adopted — that measurement happened (2026-07-25, see Step A) and
267	  Step A did not pan out: neither available lever fixes the problem,
268	  one of them (disabled thinking) actively breaks structured-output
269	  compliance. Step B is therefore the operative mechanism for whatever
270	  truncation risk remains after Decision 1's relevance filtering, not a
271	  fallback that might prove unnecessary.
272	- Decision 1's relevance filtering is now confirmed, independent of the
273	  Step A result, to remove real cost: in the reconstructed failing
274	  request, one excluded entity (`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md`,
275	  judged `peripheral`) carried ~53KB of existing content — more than the
276	  other nine targets combined. Filtering it out doesn't just reduce entity
277	  *count*, it removes the single largest driver of expected output size
278	  from the batch entirely.
279	- Revision-call count becomes variable per run instead of fixed at one
280	  once Step B lands, bounded by a fixed recursion-depth ceiling (proposed:
281	  3) rather than unbounded — most enrichments still cost exactly one call;
282	  a run whose survivors genuinely overflow the budget pays for a bounded
283	  number of extra calls, not an open-ended fan-out. "Bounded" is not
284	  "small": depth 3 with per-node doubling retry means a worst-case run can
285	  still cost on the order of 15-30 model calls. The ceiling caps the
286	  failure mode, it is not a latency guarantee.
287	- The relevance-threshold warning this ADR introduces (Decision 1) differs
288	  from the DAG's existing `proposal.warnings` uses in one respect worth
289	  naming honestly: the existing cases (a missing target file, a failed
290	  resolution call) are anomaly signals that fire rarely, so a user has
291	  reason to read one when it appears. This warning is expected to fire
292	  routinely — most sources touching several tangential entities will
293	  produce one on every run — which is a faster path to it becoming
294	  background noise a user learns to skim past. This is a known, accepted
295	  UX risk, not something this ADR resolves; its long-term visibility to
296	  the user hasn't been validated.
297	- `ModelContractError` needs a structured way to distinguish truncation
298	  from validation failure before Step B can be implemented safely; this is
299	  a prerequisite, not yet done, and is testable deterministically (a
300	  scripted fake client), not a live-model concern.
301	- This does not eliminate truncation risk outright: a single entity whose
302	  own existing note is large enough to overflow the budget by itself, or a
303	  batch that still fails at the recursion-depth ceiling, is a real,
304	  surfaced failure (a warning naming the affected entities) — not
305	  silently papered over, and not infinitely retried.
306	- `EntityResolutionOutput` (the resolution call, one step earlier in the
307	  DAG) shares the same single-call-for-every-entity shape this ADR treats
308	  as risky for the revision call, and Decision 1 adds output to every
309	  entity in it. It is explicitly out of scope here — its per-entity output
310	  is much smaller (no full-note regeneration) and it has not been observed
311	  to truncate in practice — but that is a known, accepted gap, not an
312	  oversight: if it is ever observed to fail the same way, it should get
313	  the same sequenced treatment (direct fix first, bounded adaptive
314	  batching second), not a redesign from scratch.
315	
316	## Sources

319	  validation error may mean the model response was truncated, not

Adding `register: Literal["formal", "casual"] | None = Field(...)` to a Pydantic `BaseModel` subclass produced `UserWarning: Field name "register" in "CandidateMemoryModel" shadows an attribute in parent "BaseModel"` on every import, plus a broken `INSERT` once the same name was mirrored onto the SQLAlchemy `Memory` model mid-refactor. Cause: Pydantic's `ModelMetaclass` inherits from `abc.ABCMeta`, which defines a `register` classmethod (for registering virtual subclasses) — a field named `register` shadows it at the class level. Instances still work correctly (`model.register` reads the field, not the classmethod), so this is easy to miss in a quick manual check; only the warning (or a linter treating warnings as errors) surfaces it.

If a Pydantic model needs a field for a "register"/"category"/"kind of speech" concept, don't use that literal name — this codebase uses `stance` instead (kept consistent on the paired SQLAlchemy column and dataclass too, to avoid a translation layer at the ORM boundary), with `register` reserved for user-facing vocabulary only (CLI flag `--register`, display column), mirroring the existing `--type` → `memory_type` precedent (`type` collides with Python's builtin the same way). Before naming any new Pydantic field, a quick sanity check — define a throwaway `class T(BaseModel): <name>: str | None = None` and watch for a `UserWarning` — catches this class of collision (also applies to `copy`, `dict`, `json`, `schema`, and other `BaseModel`/`ABCMeta` method names) before it reaches a migration or a real model.

### `mentions` relationship edges inherit the same per-worktree "last indexed wins" property as `Note.content_hash`

**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Source:** PR #29 (`relationship-graph-traversal-9xnnu9`), `_sync_note_mentions` in `src/wakil/app/workspace_service.py`

`index_notes` extracts `[[wikilink]]`s from each note body it sees on disk into `mentions` `Relationship` rows (ADR 0006 Phase 1), and `_sync_note_mentions` deliberately leaves notes absent from the current checkout's `present_paths` untouched — this is correct and already documented in its own docstring, so a note that only exists on another branch doesn't have its edges wrongly pruned. But the corollary is the same underlying property as the "Git worktrees fix the ingest lock race, but wakil's workspace identity isn't worktree-aware" entry above, one level down: a note's `mentions` edges reflect whichever worktree last ran `index_notes` against it, exactly like `Note.content_hash`/frontmatter already only reflect the last-indexed worktree's version of that file's content. Two linked worktrees on divergent branches, sharing one `state_root`-keyed database, will have the more-recently-indexed worktree's link graph for a shared note "win" — not a new bug, just the existing single-writer-view property extending into the new relationship table now that one exists.

This isn't a regression PR #29 introduced (the `Note` row's own `content_hash`/frontmatter already had this property before any `Relationship` table existed) and there's no reported symptom yet — recorded here so that if `wakil relationships`/backlink output ever looks stale or one-sided for a note actively edited across two worktrees, the first thing to check is which worktree most recently ran `index_notes` against that note, not the traversal query itself.

### An adversarial-review subagent's isolation checkouts left the working tree in detached HEAD

**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Source:** PR #27 (`feat/memory-register-phase-2`), round-2 adversarial review

A review subagent verified "each of the 4 commits builds/passes standalone" by running `git log`/`git show --stat`/`git checkout <sha>` experiments on the branch directly (its own suggested verification method), but never checked back out to the branch tip afterward. The next actor (the main session, continuing on the same checkout) resumed work believing it was still on `feat/memory-register-phase-2`, and `git branch --show-current` returned empty — a plain `git status`/`git diff` looked deceptively normal (a detached HEAD at an ancestor commit still shows real, correctly-tracked files, just an older subset of them), and a test file that should have had four fixture memories and a `--register` test appeared to have only three and none, which read at first glance like a mysteriously reverted change rather than "wrong commit checked out entirely." Caught by noticing `git branch --show-current` was empty and `git log --oneline -1 -- <file>` pointed at an old commit, not by anything failing loudly.

No harm resulted here — the actual branch pointer (`feat/memory-register-phase-2`) was never moved, only the working tree's checkout target, so `git checkout <branch-name>` recovered instantly with the later uncommitted edit carried forward intact. But the lesson generalizes: any agent (subagent or main session) that checks out a specific commit SHA to test/inspect it in isolation must checkout back to the branch name before finishing or handing off — `git checkout <sha>` for verification should be immediately followed by `git checkout <branch>`, and the safer alternative when only running tests against an old commit is a disposable `git worktree add` rather than moving the shared checkout's HEAD at all.

The ADR is updated and pushed. Here's the synthesis of the whole path through this problem:

**What actually holds up, in priority order:**

1. **Relevance filtering (Decision 1, implemented) is the primary fix, not a nice-to-have.** The live experiment proved this concretely, not just in principle: `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` alone — a 53KB note, correctly judged `peripheral` by the resolution step — was bigger than the other nine target notes combined. Excluding it removes the single largest cost driver in the batch before any expensive call happens, at zero added model calls. This is doing more real work than anything in Decision 2.

2. **Step A (bound `thinking` via `effort` or disable it) is dead — don't build anything around it.** Tested live against the real failing shape: `effort=low` changed thinking-token spend by 0.6% (not a lever that does anything here), and disabling thinking traded the token-budget problem for a harder, contract-breaking failure (unparseable prose instead of JSON) even with budget to spare. content.text:
Very informative, and it resolves the open question decisively.

**Relevance filtering worked as designed but did not fully solve it.** 6 entities were correctly excluded (`Brian Corr`, `Jake McGuire`, `Prabhuddha Bhan`, `Murtaza Mister` as `minor`; `Mosaic`, `Scorealytics News Accuracy Framework`) — but the remaining batch of just **4** `central` entities (Lawrence Krubner, Edward Bridges, Scorealytics, Scorealytics AI Mentoring Program) **still truncated** at `max_tokens=16384`, only 3,783 chars generated before cutoff. This is a real, live confirmation that Step B is genuinely necessary, not hypothetically necessary — relevance filtering shrank the problem but didn't eliminate it. (The command's "Aborted" at the end is benign — it hit the interactive y/N confirmation prompt with no terminal attached in the background run, not a new failure.)

One more thing worth flagging: this run rated **Brian Corr as `minor`**, while your own hand-labeled case study called him "very relevant" (mapped to `central`). That's the exact run-to-run judgment inconsistency the adversarial reviewer's point #7 warned about — concrete evidence for it now exists, not just a theoretical risk.

Let me fold both findings into the ADR.

181	    length (the batch's single largest note is isolated into its own half

class ModelContractError(RuntimeError):
    """The model failed to produce schema-valid output twice in a row."""

    def __init__(self, contract: str, detail: str, *, truncated: bool):
        self.contract = contract
        self.detail = detail
        # Distinguishes "kept hitting max_tokens" from "kept producing
        # malformed JSON" — only the former is something a caller can
        # meaningfully react to (e.g. by splitting a batch and retrying;
        # see ADR 0015). A validation failure will recur identically on a
        # smaller request for an unrelated reason, so it isn't.
        self.truncated = truncated
        super().__init__(f"{contract}: model output failed validation twice: {detail}")

def _split_candidates_by_content_length(
    candidates: list[_EntityCandidate],
) -> tuple[list[_EntityCandidate], list[_EntityCandidate]]:
    """Greedy 2-way balance by existing-note content length (longest-first):
    the single largest note is placed first, then each remaining candidate
    joins whichever half currently has less total content. Isolates the
    biggest cost driver from compounding with the next-biggest, rather than
    blind index-order halving — see ADR 0015, Decision 2 Step B."""
    ordered = sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: len(c[2]), reverse=True)
    half_a: list[_EntityCandidate] = []
    half_b: list[_EntityCandidate] = []
    size_a = size_b = 0
    for candidate in ordered:
        content_len = len(candidate[2])
        if size_a <= size_b:
            half_a.append(candidate)
            size_a += content_len
        else:
            half_b.append(candidate)
            size_b += content_len
    return half_a, half_b


def _apply_entity_revisions(
    proposal: EnrichmentProposal, candidates: list[_EntityCandidate], revisions: list[EntityRevision]
) -> None:
    today = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()
    by_path = {res.target_note_path: content for res, _, content in candidates}
    for revision in revisions:
        old_content = by_path.get(revision.target_note_path)
        if old_content is None or not revision.has_update:
            continue
        new_content = _merge_entity_note(old_content, revision, today)
        if new_content is None:
            proposal.warnings.append(
                f"{revision.target_note_path}: doesn't match the expected H1 / "
                "'Timeline / Log' shape — update skipped, left unchanged"
            )
            continue
        if new_content == old_content:
            continue
        proposal.entity_updates.append(
            EntityUpdate(
                target_note_path=revision.target_note_path,
                old_content=old_content,
                new_content=new_content,
            )
        )


def _revise_candidates(
    config: WorkspaceConfig,
    client: ModelClient,
    text: str,
    proposal: EnrichmentProposal,
    candidates: list[_EntityCandidate],
    depth: int = 0,
) -> None:
    """Revise `candidates` in one call; on a truncated response, bisect by
    existing-note content length and retry each half, recursively, up to
    `_MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH` (ADR 0015, Decision 2 Step B). A validation
    failure (not a truncation) never triggers a split — it would recur
    identically on a smaller batch for an unrelated reason."""
    targets = [(res.target_note_path, content) for res, _, content in candidates]
    skill = load_skill("note-revision", config.root_path)
    system = build_system_prompt(skill, EntityRevisionOutput)
    cacheable_prefix, prompt = build_revision_prompt(
        text, proposal.summary, targets, context=proposal.context
    )
    try:
        result = complete_with_contract(
            client, system, prompt, EntityRevisionOutput, cacheable_prefix=cacheable_prefix
        )
    except ModelContractError as exc:
        if exc.truncated and len(candidates) > 1 and depth < _MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH:
            half_a, half_b = _split_candidates_by_content_length(candidates)
            _revise_candidates(config, client, text, proposal, half_a, depth + 1)
            _revise_candidates(config, client, text, proposal, half_b, depth + 1)
            return
        count = len(candidates)
        entity_word = "entity" if count == 1 else "entities"
        proposal.warnings.append(
            f"Entity updates failed while revising {count} {entity_word} in one call "
            f"({', '.join(res.name for res, _, _ in candidates)}); "
            f"existing notes left unchanged: {exc}"
        )
        return

    _apply_entity_revisions(proposal, candidates, result.revisions)

def _candidate(name: str, content_len: int):
    resolution = EntityResolution(name=name, entity_type="person", action="update")
    return (resolution, Path(f"people/{name}.md"), "x" * content_len)


def test_split_by_content_length_isolates_largest_into_its_own_half():
    candidates = [_candidate("a", 10), _candidate("b", 5), _candidate("c", 100), _candidate("d", 3)]
    half_a, half_b = _split_candidates_by_content_length(candidates)

    names_a = {c[0].name for c in half_a}
    names_b = {c[0].name for c in half_b}
    assert names_a | names_b == {"a", "b", "c", "d"}
    assert names_a & names_b == set()
    assert names_a == {"c"}  # the single largest, alone
    assert names_b == {"a", "b", "d"}


def test_split_by_content_length_balances_total_size_not_count():
    candidates = [_candidate("a", 100), _candidate("b", 1), _candidate("c", 1), _candidate("d", 1)]
    half_a, half_b = _split_candidates_by_content_length(candidates)

    assert sum(len(c[2]) for c in half_a) == 100
    assert sum(len(c[2]) for c in half_b) == 3


def test_split_by_content_length_two_candidates_splits_one_each():
    half_a, half_b = _split_candidates_by_content_length([_candidate("a", 10), _candidate("b", 5)])
    assert len(half_a) == 1
    assert len(half_b) == 1


# A note shaped like REAL_SHAPED_PERSON but padded to be dramatically larger
# than a typical target note — for exercising which half of a bisection
# split a large note lands in.
LONG_SHAPED_PERSON = (
    "---\n"
    "type: person\n"
    "name: Alice Long\n"
    "status: active\n"
    "created: 2026-06-01\n"
    "updated: 2026-06-01\n"
    "---\n\n"
    "# alice\n\n"
    + ("Filler paragraph to inflate this note's existing content length. " * 100)
    + "\n\n---\n\n"
    "## Timeline / Log\n\n"
    "### 2026-06-01 — history\n"
    "- Some prior detail.\n"
)


def test_entity_updates_bisect_and_recover_after_truncation(workspace, transcript, kb_path):
    _write_person(kb_path, "alice", content=LONG_SHAPED_PERSON)
    _write_person(kb_path, "bob")
    _write_person(kb_path, "carol")
    resolution = {
        "entities": [
            {
                "name": slug.title(),
                "entity_type": "person",
                "action": "update",
                "target_note_path": f"people/{slug}.md",
                "confidence": 0.9,
                "relevance": "central",
            }
            for slug in ("alice", "bob", "carol")
        ]
    }
    alice_revision = {
        "revisions": [
            {
                "target_note_path": "people/alice.md",
                "has_update": True,
                "compiled_truth": "Alice updated truth.",
                "timeline_entry": "### 2026-07-16 — alice update\n- detail",
            }
        ]
    }
    bob_carol_revision = {
        "revisions": [
            {
                "target_note_path": "people/bob.md",
                "has_update": True,
                "compiled_truth": "Bob updated truth.",
                "timeline_entry": "### 2026-07-16 — bob update\n- detail",
            },
            {
                "target_note_path": "people/carol.md",
                "has_update": True,
                "compiled_truth": "Carol updated truth.",
                "timeline_entry": "### 2026-07-16 — carol update\n- detail",
            },
        ]
    }
    source_id = _capture(workspace, transcript)
    client = FakeClient(
        [
            MODEL_JSON,
            resolution,
            # First (unsplit) attempt truncates twice -> triggers a split.
            ModelTruncatedError(max_tokens=8192, partial="{"),
            ModelTruncatedError(max_tokens=16384, partial="{"),
            # alice, isolated as the largest note, succeeds alone.
            alice_revision,
            # bob + carol, the smaller remainder, succeed together.
            bob_carol_revision,
        ]
    )

    proposal = prepare_enrichment(workspace, source_id, client)

    assert {u.target_note_path for u in proposal.entity_updates} == {
        "people/alice.md",
        "people/bob.md",
        "people/carol.md",
    }
    assert not any("failed while revising" in warning for warning in proposal.warnings)
    assert len(client.calls) == 6


def test_entity_updates_stop_bisecting_at_depth_ceiling(workspace, transcript, kb_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(ingest_service, "_MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH", 1)
    _write_person(kb_path, "dan")
    _write_person(kb_path, "erin")
    resolution = {
        "entities": [
            {
                "name": slug.title(),
                "entity_type": "person",
                "action": "update",
                "target_note_path": f"people/{slug}.md",
                "confidence": 0.9,
                "relevance": "central",
            }
            for slug in ("dan", "erin")
        ]
    }
    source_id = _capture(workspace, transcript)
    # Every revision attempt truncates, at every depth: 2 (top) + 2 (each of
    # the 2 leaf sub-batches once split) = 6 truncations after extraction
    # and resolution.
    client = FakeClient(
        [MODEL_JSON, resolution]
        + [ModelTruncatedError(max_tokens=8192, partial="{") for _ in range(6)]
    )

    proposal = prepare_enrichment(workspace, source_id, client)

    assert proposal.entity_updates == []
    failure_warnings = [w for w in proposal.warnings if "failed while revising" in w]
    # Split once (depth 0 -> 1), then the ceiling stops further splitting:
    # two separate single-entity failures, not one two-entity failure and
    # not unbounded further recursion.
    assert len(failure_warnings) == 2
    assert any("Dan" in w for w in failure_warnings)
    assert any("Erin" in w for w in failure_warnings)
    assert len(client.calls) == 8


def test_entity_updates_validation_failure_does_not_trigger_split(workspace, transcript, kb_path):

def test_complete_with_contract_raises_after_second_truncation():
    client = _ScriptedClient(
        [
            ModelTruncatedError(max_tokens=8192, partial='{"value": "cut off'),
            ModelTruncatedError(max_tokens=16384, partial='{"value": "still cut off'),
        ]
    )
    with pytest.raises(ModelContractError) as exc_info:
        complete_with_contract(client, "sys", "prompt", _Output)
    assert "truncated" in str(exc_info.value)
    assert "max_tokens=16384" in str(exc_info.value)
    # Callers (e.g. entity-revision bisection, ADR 0015) branch on this to

    assert exc_info.value.truncated is True


def test_complete_with_contract_raises_after_second_invalid_response():
    client = _ScriptedClient(["not json", "still not json"])
    with pytest.raises(ModelContractError) as exc_info:
        complete_with_contract(client, "sys", "prompt", _Output)
    # A validation failure would recur identically on a smaller request for
    # an unrelated reason, so callers must not treat it like a truncation.
    assert exc_info.value.truncated is False

8	# Periodic Entity Compilation and Gated Timeline-Context Trimming
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	`wakil enrich`'s entity-revision call (`_run_entity_updates` /
13	`_revise_candidates`, `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`) inlines the
14	**entire current file content** of every candidate entity note into the

16	notes only grow — Timeline is append-only by design
17	(`note-revision/SKILL.md`) — so this cost is unbounded.
18	`docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md`
19	already diagnosed a real `ModelTruncatedError` from this (case study:
20	`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` ~53KB, `people/edward-bridges.md`
21	~32KB) and landed two *reactive* mitigations: relevance-gating candidates
22	before the call, and bisecting a batch by content length after a truncation
23	occurs. Both work around the size; neither reduces it. ADR 0015's own
24	Consequences section names the gap directly: "a single entity whose own
25	existing note is large enough to overflow the budget by itself... is a
26	real, surfaced failure" — not solved by either of its mechanisms.
27	
28	Separately, `docs/entity-model.md` (a design doc, not yet implemented)
29	already proposes a `wakil entity compile <slug>` command: re-synthesize
30	Compiled Truth from durable memory, diff-preview, commit — but scoped to
31	one entity and assuming a DB-row-backed Timeline model (ADR 0005) that
32	isn't actually wired up. Its own audit of the real vault found "Compiled
33	Truth is empty for most of the vault... well over a hundred lines of raw,
34	unsynthesized interview notes dumped into Timeline instead" — the
35	synthesis half of the two-part format has never actually run for most
36	entities.
37	
38	This ADR proposes the proactive complement ADR 0015 names as still needed:
39	keep entity notes themselves smaller in the places that matter for context
40	cost, rather than only working around their size after the fact.
41	
42	## Decision
43	
44	Two mechanisms, shipped together.
45	
46	**1. `wakil entities compile [SLUG]`** — a new periodic/on-demand command
47	that re-synthesizes each entity's Compiled Truth from its full Timeline
48	history, favoring recency: recent entries keep concrete detail; older
49	entries collapse to the facts that still matter, dropping stale specifics
50	(a scheduled call that already happened, a "next steps" note superseded by
51	a later entry). Timeline itself is never touched by this operation —
52	it stays the complete, intact evidence log. Generalizes
53	`docs/entity-model.md`'s single-entity design into a workspace-wide sweep,
54	since "periodic" implies batch:
55	
56	- No `SLUG`: workspace-wide due-scan (the periodic use case).
57	- `SLUG` given: compile that one entity now, ignoring the due-check (manual
58	  override, e.g. right after a big meeting).
59	- `--type`, `--min-timeline-chars`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--commit` flags,
60	  mirroring `wakil schema migrate`'s existing plan/diff/confirm/apply shape
61	  (`schema_migrate_service.py`, `main.py:897-970`) — the closest existing
62	  precedent for a workspace-wide, non-source-scoped maintenance operation
63	  with a reviewable diff.
64	
65	**2. Gated context-trimming**: once a note has been compiled at least once,
66	`wakil enrich`'s revision call sends only its Compiled Truth (not Timeline)
67	as context — directly attacking the size that caused the original
68	truncation. This is conditional, not universal: since most existing entity
69	notes have empty/placeholder Compiled Truth today, trimming unconditionally
70	would blind enrichment to most of what's actually known about most
71	entities until the whole vault has been compiled. The trim applies only to
72	notes carrying a fresh `compiled_through` marker (see below); everything
73	else keeps today's full-content behavior as a safe fallback. This couples
74	the two mechanisms by design: the context-cost benefit is earned per-note
75	by having run `entities compile` on it, not granted unconditionally. On a
76	freshly-migrated vault (nothing compiled yet), `wakil enrich` behaves
77	exactly as it does today — zero regression risk on day one — and cost
78	shrinks precisely as compilation coverage grows.
79	
80	### Mechanism 1 (shared prerequisite): factor the note-section split out
81	
82	`_merge_entity_note` already parses a note into "top section" (between H1
83	and the Timeline heading) and "Timeline section" via `_H1_RE` /
84	`_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE` (`ingest_service.py:1016-1085`). Factor this into a
85	reusable `_split_note_sections(content) -> tuple[Post, h1_line, top, timeline] | None`
86	helper, used by the merge path, the new compile path, and the gated
87	context-trim. Pure refactor — `_merge_entity_note`'s own behavior is
88	unchanged.
89	
90	### Mechanism 2 detail: `entities compile`
91	
92	- **New skill** `src/wakil/skills/entity-compile/SKILL.md`, distinct from
93	  `note-revision` — the judgment is genuinely different. `note-revision`
94	  merges *new* source material and treats "shorter than before" as a red
95	  flag; compile has no new source, re-derives Compiled Truth from the
96	  note's own full Timeline, and shortening old, superseded detail is the
97	  point, provided every still-true fact remains present somewhere (Compiled
98	  Truth or the untouched Timeline). Requires an `eval.json` live-model
99	  scenario before being considered production-ready, per this project's own
100	  norm for new judgment guidance (ADR 0004) — not just unit tests.
101	- **New contract** `EntityCompileOutput` (`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`): one
102	  `compiled_truth: str` field. One entity per call, deliberately not
103	  batched like the revision call — there's no shared cacheable prefix
104	  across unrelated entities' Timelines the way there is across candidates
105	  sharing one enrich source document, so batching here buys nothing and
106	  reintroduces the exact truncation risk this ADR exists to reduce. Each
107	  call's size is bounded by that single note's own content, not compounded
108	  across entities. The residual risk of one pathologically long Timeline
109	  overflowing a single call is real (named in ADR 0015) and left as a
110	  surfaced warning, not solved by new chunking logic here.
111	- **New prompt builder** `build_compile_prompt(top_section, timeline_section)`
112	  in `llm/prompts.py` — simpler than `build_revision_prompt`, no source
113	  document or cacheable-prefix split needed.
114	- **New frontmatter field** `compiled_through: <date>`, stamped by
115	  `entities compile`, meaning "Compiled Truth already reflects every
116	  Timeline entry as of this date." Distinct from `updated:`, which is
117	  stamped on any content change including a plain Timeline append during
118	  `wakil enrich` and so can't distinguish "just grew" from "was actively
119	  re-synthesized." Due-check: never compiled and Timeline exceeds
120	  `--min-timeline-chars` (default TBD at implementation, e.g. 4000 —
121	  Timeline character length as a computable proxy for cost, the same
122	  precedent `_split_candidates_by_content_length` already established); or
123	  compiled before, but new entries past `compiled_through` push accumulated
124	  growth over that same threshold.
125	- **New service module** `src/wakil/app/entity_compile_service.py`
126	  (mirrors `schema_migrate_service.py`'s shape: `plan_entity_compilation`/
127	  `apply_entity_compilation`, own `CompileProposal`/`CompilePlan`
128	  dataclasses) rather than growing the already-1450-line
129	  `ingest_service.py` further. `apply_entity_compilation` re-reads each
130	  file immediately before writing and skips (reports, doesn't silently
131	  overwrite) anything changed since planning — the same stale-file guard
132	  `apply_migrations`/`apply_enrichment` already use. Reuses
133	  `_merge_entity_note`'s top-section-replace logic for the actual write,
134	  with `compiled_through` added to `frontmatter_updates` alongside
135	  `updated`; Timeline section passed through byte-identical.
136	- **New CLI group** `entities_app`, `app.add_typer(entities_app,
137	  name="entities")` — plural, matching the existing `sources` group
138	  precedent. `--commit` reuses the existing `"chore"` commit kind
139	  (`git_service.commit_change`), no `COMMIT_PREFIXES` change needed — same
140	  category as `schema migrate --commit`.
141	
142	### Mechanism 2 detail: gated trim in the revision call
143	
144	In `_run_entity_updates`, when building `candidates`, also read each
145	target's `compiled_through` frontmatter and Timeline size. A new
146	`_is_compile_fresh(post, timeline_section, min_timeline_chars) -> bool`
147	gate decides, per candidate, whether `build_revision_prompt` receives that
148	target's full content (today's behavior, the default) or just its top
149	section via `_split_note_sections` (once compiled and not yet stale).
150	`_merge_entity_note`'s merge step is unaffected either way — it always
151	re-reads the full file at apply time regardless of what the model saw,
152	since merging needs the real Timeline to prepend into.
153	
154	### Passive nudge from `wakil enrich`
155	
156	When `_run_entity_updates` touches a candidate whose Timeline has grown
157	past `min_timeline_chars` since its last `compiled_through` (or was never
158	compiled and already exceeds it), add one batched `proposal.warnings`
159	entry: "N entities have grown large enough to benefit from compilation —
160	run `wakil entities compile`." Visible, never auto-triggered — the same
161	advisory pattern already used for relevance exclusions and stale-file
162	skips, consistent with `CLAUDE.md`'s "avoid hidden background behavior."
163	
164	## Alternatives considered
165	
166	- **Trim Timeline from every candidate's context unconditionally,
167	  immediately.** Rejected: the real vault audit in `docs/entity-model.md`
168	  found Compiled Truth empty/placeholder for most existing entity notes —
169	  an unconditional trim would blind enrichment to most of what's actually
170	  known about most entities until a full-vault compile sweep completes.
171	  Gating per-note on `compiled_through` avoids any regression window at the
172	  cost of the benefit phasing in gradually rather than landing all at once.
173	- **Batch multiple entities per compile call**, mirroring
174	  `_revise_candidates`'s bisection shape. Rejected: that batching exists
175	  because many candidates share one cached source-document prefix during
176	  `wakil enrich`; no equivalent shared prefix exists across unrelated
177	  entities' Timelines during a compile sweep, so batching adds truncation
178	  risk without a caching benefit to offset it. One call per entity keeps
179	  each call's size bounded by a single note.
180	- **Drive Timeline entries off `Memory` rows (ADR 0005) instead of parsing
181	  Markdown directly**, to get a structured, queryable due-check for free.
182	  Rejected for this ADR: ADR 0005's `event_date`-backed model is accepted
183	  but not implemented — nothing in `apply_enrichment` currently links a
184	  `Memory` row to the literal Timeline text prepended into a note. Building
185	  this ADR's due-check against real Markdown (the same source
186	  `_merge_entity_note` already parses) ships against what actually exists;
187	  converging with ADR 0005 later is a separate, still-open decision, not a
188	  blocker here.
189	- **A `page_versions`/snapshot table to make compilation reversible at the
190	  DB layer.** Rejected, consistent with ADR 0007 (Markdown is source of
191	  truth, git provides version history): `entities compile`'s "before" state
192	  is recoverable via `git log`/`git diff` on the note file itself, the same
193	  as every other durable-content change in this codebase.
194	
195	## Consequences
196	
197	- `wakil enrich`'s revision-call cost shrinks precisely as
198	  `entities compile` coverage grows across the vault — no benefit on day
199	  one, growing benefit as the command is run, with zero regression risk in
200	  between because untouched notes keep today's full-content behavior.
201	- A genuinely new judgment surface (`entity-compile` skill) is introduced
202	  and, per ADR 0004's own norm, is not considered production-ready until it
203	  has a live-model eval scenario — this ADR does not consider that
204	  optional polish.
205	- Timeline remains the durable, complete, human-auditable evidence log this
206	  project's principles require (`CLAUDE.md`: "do not silently rewrite user
207	  knowledge") — no mechanism here ever edits, reorders, or shortens it.
208	  Everything "compressed" is specifically the derived Compiled Truth
209	  summary, always re-synthesizable from the untouched Timeline if a past
210	  compile is ever judged wrong.
211	- A new, small vocabulary item (`compiled_through` frontmatter field) is
212	  added to `compiled-truth-timeline`-shaped entity schemas; whether this
213	  needs an explicit schema-catalog change or fits under existing permissive
214	  frontmatter validation needs confirming against `validate_proposal` at
215	  implementation time.
216	- Residual truncation risk is not fully eliminated: a single entity whose
217	  own Timeline is large enough to overflow one compile call by itself is
218	  left as a surfaced warning, not new chunking logic — the same class of
219	  gap ADR 0015 already accepted for the revision call, not solved by either
220	  ADR.
221	- This does not converge with ADR 0005's `Memory`-backed Timeline-entry
222	  model; both remain accepted-but-not-unified designs until a later,
223	  separate decision reconciles them.
224	
225	## Sources
226	
227	- `docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md`
228	  (the reactive mitigations this ADR complements; names the "single large
229	  entity" gap this ADR still doesn't close)
230	- `docs/entity-model.md` (`wakil entity compile <slug>` design origin; the
231	  "Compiled Truth is empty for most of the vault" audit finding driving the
232	  gated-rollout decision)
233	- `docs/adr/0005-timeline-entries-as-memory-rows.md` (considered and
234	  deliberately not converged with, see Alternatives)
235	- `docs/adr/0007-markdown-source-of-truth-sqlite-operational-store.md`
236	  (why no snapshot table)
237	- `docs/adr/0004-exclude-live-model-skill-evals-from-default-ci.md` (the
238	  live-eval norm this ADR's new skill is held to)
239	- `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `_run_entity_updates`,
240	  `_merge_entity_note`, `_split_candidates_by_content_length`
241	- `src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py` (the plan/apply/stale-guard
242	  shape this ADR's new service module follows)
243	- `src/wakil/skills/note-revision/SKILL.md` (State vs. Timeline discipline
244	  the new `entity-compile` skill deliberately diverges from, and why)
245	- `CLAUDE.md`, "Working Agreement for Agents" (11: show reviewable diffs;
246	  12: do not silently rewrite user knowledge) and "Design Biases" (avoid
247	  hidden background behavior)
